m.d: If you even something (out/up), you reduce the ups and downs; you make it smooth or equal.
m.e: India was leading 2-1, but Australia evened the score in the last minute.

m.d: If you even a problem out, you solve it.
m.e: I went down and evened it all out. Everyone's happy now.

m.d: If things are even, the top or surface of each is as high as the others.
m.e: The top of the wall is even because the bricks are all the same size.

m.d: If a number is even, it can be divided into 2 equal parts.
m.e: 2, 4, 6 and 8 are even numbers. 1, 3, 5 and 7 are not even numbers; they are odd numbers.

m.d: You use even to focus on the most surprising or unlikely case.
With preposition phrases:
m.e: Even in peaceful countries, there are problems.

m.d: With noun phrases:
m.e: Everyone walks to school here, even the teachers.

m.d: Everything is all that exists, or all things in one area.
m.e: If you win, you get everything: the car and all other prizes you won!

m.d: If I ask you if you have ever been to France, I am asking if you have been to France at any time in your life.
m.e: Have you ever met a king or queen?

m.d: Ever may also mean always.
m.e: I will love you forever and ever.

m.d: all the people, things, times, etc.
m.e: I work every day from 6:00 to 9:30.

m.d: All (the) people; every person.
All (the) people.
Period from dusk to midnight.
m.e: We eat a big meal in the evening.

m.d: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.
m.e: The gun is evidence that professor Pickle killed Mr. Mustard.

m.d: In a courtroom, evidence refers to anything that is shown to the judge that is related to the case during a trial.
When you evidence something, you provide evidence or the truth of an event.
m.e: Something good must have happened to her, as evidenced by the smile on her face.

m.d: The quality of being evil; evilness.
m.e: He was so full of evil I do not think he knew what good was.

m.d: Something that causes harm, or harm itself.
m.e: We faced many evils on our journey.

m.d: The source or cause of evil as a spiritual or supernatural force. This is often called true evil.
m.e: I have seen things that lead me to believe that real evil exists.

m.d: The opposite of good, if something is evil it is very far from good or is against good. This usually means behaving in a way that is not moral or not ethical.
m.e: Hitler was a very evil person.

m.d: (at, to, or in) every place
m.e: I've looked everywhere else, so it must be here.

m.d: An event is anything that happens.
m.e: The event of her walking into the room happened before the event of the book falling off the table, so she saw it fall.

m.d: An event is when many people come together at a time they choose for a reason or for fun.
m.e: At the event tomorrow we're going to have balloons and music.

m.d: If something will happen eventually, it will happen but it will be in the future, not soon. Some day it will happen.
m.e: I'll clean out my closet eventually.

m.d: The day or night before, usually used for holidays.
m.e: My parents always let me open one gift on Christmas Eve.

m.d: Evening.
m.e: One the eve of our wedding anniversary, I give my wife a red rose.

m.d: Eve is a female given name.
something that is done a lot or happens a lot; something that is ordinary
m.e: These are my everyday clothes.

m.d: Evan is a male given name.
Evan is a surname.
Evolution is the process of slow change.
m.e: The theory of evolution is the basis of modern biology.

m.d: An evolution is a change that happens over time.
m.e: Over the last ten years, there has been an evolution in the way we think about this disease.

m.d: Evans is a surname.
If you evacuate, you leave because of danger.
m.e: The firefighters told everyone to evacuate the burning building.

m.d: If something is evidently true or has evidently happened, it is clear or obvious to see.
m.e: She was evidently upset by the news.

m.d: If something is evidently true or has evidently happened, it seems to be true based on what is known.
m.e: Evidently, they forgot to lock the door.'''

m.d: Evacuation is the act of evacuating.
m.e: There was an emergency evacuation when the fire alarm rang.

m.d: Evaluation is the process of making a judgement.
m.e: If a teacher doesn't know the student well, it makes the evaluation of the student's level very difficult.

m.d: An evaluation is a judgement.
m.e: Lamont Library’s 24-hour service received a positive evaluation this past spring.

m.d: If something is everlasting then it lasts forever.
If something evolves, it, or things of its kind, change slowly over a long time or from generation to generation.
m.e: Because computer technology evolves rapidly, a product may have changed before most people learn about it.

m.d: Something that is related to evolution.
m.e: Humans have a long and complicated evolutionary history.

m.d: If something is evident it is very easy to realize or understand.
m.e: It is evident that he is angry by looking at his facial expression.

m.d: If you evaluate someone or something, you judge it.
m.e: It is difficult to evaluate the effectiveness of the LINK programme, but we believe it has been useful.

m.d: If a person is being evasive, they speak in a way that avoids an issue.
An eviction is the action of expelling someone from a property.
If you evade something, then you try to avoid it or keep away from it.
If something is evenly spread, it is spread out as to form a flat surface.
m.e: Spread the icing evenly over the cake.

m.d: If you distribute something evenly, you give the same amount of it to everyone.
m.e: To avoid arguments, he divided the sweets evenly between his two children.

m.d: If a number is evenly divisible, it can be divided to leave no remainder.
An evasion is the action of evading something.
m.e: block evasion

m.d: If you evict someone, you take their home from them.
m.e: The council evicted the man because he didn't pay his rent.
